tagline: A loop from US 42 reaches Westport on the Ohio River.
intro: Highway 524 Loop leaves US 42 between Goshen and Sligo, passes through Westport and rejoins the same highway. The Ohio River is the destination at Westport, an unincorporated community in Oldham County.
The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet recorded the loop’s scenic designation on February 24, 2011. Westport’s postal history reaches back much farther: its post office opened on November 29, 1815.
Follow KY 524 from US 42 to Westport, then continue along the loop to return to US 42. The state highway stays within Oldham County for its 12.148-mile course.

moments.title: Westport landing
moments.text: Westport stands along the Ohio River, with a post office whose opening dates to November 29, 1815. The unincorporated community had 253 residents in the 2020 census. KY 524 passes through town between its two junctions with US 42.

moments.title: Reuben Sale House
moments.text: The Reuben Sale House is a brick landmark on Smith Lane near La Grange, built around 1833. Its two stories have four bays, with Flemish-bond brickwork on the front. A double-crib log barn forms a second contributing building in its National Register designation, recorded in 1982.

moments.title: Bethlehem, Indiana
moments.text: Bethlehem lies across the Ohio River from Oldham County, in Indiana. Platted in 1812, the community was laid out in a rectangle of 124 lots. Its steamboat and ferry landing, together with roads to New Washington and Lexington, once made it a transportation center. By 1900, ferry service had ended. The 1937 Ohio River flood destroyed much of the town’s historical record. A later preservation effort began with Historic Bethlehem Inc. in 1993, which converted the old elementary school into a community center and started the Autumn on the River festival.
